=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py
Line or code reference: Line 633 and line 719
Problem: Both exception handlers bind `exc` via `except Exception as exc` but never reference the variable.
Why it fails at runtime: The CI lint job exits with code 1, blocking PR merge.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- File: .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml, .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
Line or code reference: The test allowlists in each workflow (around lines 191-198 in ci.yml, etc.)
Problem: Two new standalone test modules — `tests/test_review_conflict_resolve_retry_state.py` and `tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_tiers.py` — are not included in any CI workflow test allowlist.
Why it fails at runtime: The standalone contract tests never execute in CI, so regressions in the retry-state signature logic, tier selection, or downgrade-marker emission are silently undetected.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- File: scripts/drift_audit.sh
Line or code reference: Function `_recheck_cluster` at approximately lines 525-570
Problem: The `_recheck_cluster` function short-circuits with `resolved=False` for any cluster that lacks a `FINGERPRINT_QUARANTINED_V1` marker.
Why it fails at runtime: A cluster that has only `PRE_EXISTING_FINGERPRINT_DRIFT_V1` markers but an existing open tracker issue never gets re-evaluated for resolution.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
Line or code reference: Function `_attempt_branch_rebuild_after_escalation`, approximately lines 4400-4620
Problem: The destructive delete/recreate flow (`gh api -X DELETE` followed by `gh api -X POST .../git/refs`) has no distributed lock or lease on the integration branch.
Why it fails at runtime: Two concurrent poll ticks could both delete the same branch ref; the second recreate could happen against a different base SHA and duplicate commits.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
